title: Function
primary_statement: f assigns to each x in D exactly one f(x)

title: Natural number
primary_statement: Peano: 1 in N; successor; induction

title: Principle of induction
primary_statement: if S contains 1 and is successor-closed then S = N

title: The ordered field Q
primary_statement: Q is an ordered field, not complete

title: Ordered field
primary_statement: field axioms + total order compatible with + and *

title: Absolute value
primary_statement: |x| = x if x>=0 else -x

title: Upper bound
primary_statement: u is an upper bound of A if a <= u for all a in A

title: Supremum
primary_statement: sup A is the least upper bound of A

title: Infimum
primary_statement: inf A is the greatest lower bound of A

title: Least-upper-bound axiom
primary_statement: every nonempty subset of R bounded above has a supremum in R

title: Completeness of R
primary_statement: R is an ordered field satisfying lub_axiom

title: Archimedean property
primary_statement: for every x in R there is n in N with n > x

title: Density of Q in R
primary_statement: between any two reals lies a rational

title: Interval
primary_statement: a subset I of R such that x,y in I, x<z<y implies z in I

title: Nested interval theorem
primary_statement: a decreasing sequence of nonempty closed bounded intervals has nonempty intersection

title: Sequence
primary_statement: a function x : N -> R

title: Convergence of a sequence
primary_statement: forall eps>0 exists N forall n>=N |x_n - L| < eps

title: Uniqueness of sequential limits
primary_statement: a convergent sequence has exactly one limit

title: Bounded sequence
primary_statement: exists M forall n |x_n| <= M

title: Convergent implies bounded
primary_statement: every convergent sequence is bounded

title: Algebra of limits
primary_statement: limits commute with + - * and / (nonzero limit)

title: Squeeze theorem
primary_statement: a_n <= x_n <= b_n and a_n,b_n -> L imply x_n -> L

title: Monotone sequence
primary_statement: nondecreasing or nonincreasing

title: Monotone convergence theorem
primary_statement: a bounded monotone real sequence converges to its sup or inf

title: Subsequence
primary_statement: x composed with a strictly increasing n_j : N -> N

title: Subsequential limit
primary_statement: a limit of some convergent subsequence

title: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem
primary_statement: every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence

title: Cauchy sequence
primary_statement: forall eps>0 exists N forall m,n>=N |x_m - x_n| < eps

title: Cauchy criterion for sequences
primary_statement: a real sequence converges iff it is Cauchy

title: Limit superior and inferior
primary_statement: limsup x_n = inf_N sup_{n>=N} x_n ; liminf dually

title: Axiom of choice
primary_statement: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Axiom of countable choice
primary_statement: a countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Infinite series
primary_statement: the formal sum of the terms of a sequence

title: Convergence of a series
primary_statement: Sigma a_n converges if the partial sums converge

title: Geometric series
primary_statement: Sigma_{n>=0} r^n = 1/(1-r) for |r| < 1

title: nth-term (divergence) test
primary_statement: if Sigma a_n converges then a_n -> 0

title: Cauchy criterion for series
primary_statement: Sigma a_n converges iff tails of partial sums are small

title: Comparison test
primary_statement: 0 <= a_n <= b_n and Sigma b_n converges imply Sigma a_n converges

title: Absolute convergence
primary_statement: Sigma a_n converges absolutely if Sigma |a_n| converges

title: Absolute convergence implies convergence
primary_statement: if Sigma |a_n| converges then Sigma a_n converges

title: Ratio test
primary_statement: limsup |a_{n+1}/a_n| < 1 implies absolute convergence

title: Root test
primary_statement: limsup |a_n|^{1/n} < 1 implies absolute convergence

title: Alternating series test
primary_statement: if b_n decreases to 0 then Sigma (-1)^n b_n converges

title: The p-series
primary_statement: Sigma 1/n^p converges iff p > 1

title: Open set
primary_statement: U is open if every point has an interval neighbourhood inside U

title: Closed set
primary_statement: A is closed if its complement is open

title: Bounded set
primary_statement: A subset of some [-M, M]

title: Limit point
primary_statement: every neighbourhood of p meets A in a point other than p

title: Closure
primary_statement: the union of A with its set of limit points

title: Closed iff sequentially closed
primary_statement: A is closed iff limits of convergent sequences in A stay in A

title: Open cover
primary_statement: a family of open sets whose union contains A

title: Compact set
primary_statement: every open cover of K has a finite subcover

title: Heine-Borel theorem
primary_statement: a subset of R is compact iff it is closed and bounded

title: Sequential compactness in R
primary_statement: K compact iff every sequence in K has a subsequence converging in K

title: Connected set
primary_statement: not the union of two disjoint nonempty relatively open sets

title: Connected subsets of R are intervals
primary_statement: A subset of R is connected iff it is an interval

title: Limit of a function
primary_statement: forall eps>0 exists delta>0 : 0<|x-c|<delta implies |f(x)-L|<eps

title: Sequential criterion for functional limits
primary_statement: lim_{x->c} f = L iff f(x_n) -> L for every x_n -> c with x_n != c

title: Continuity at a point
primary_statement: forall eps>0 exists delta>0 : |x-c|<delta implies |f(x)-f(c)|<eps

title: Continuity on a set
primary_statement: f is continuous at every point of D

title: Sequential characterization of continuity
primary_statement: f continuous at c iff f(x_n) -> f(c) whenever x_n -> c

title: Algebra of continuous functions
primary_statement: sums products quotients of continuous functions are continuous

title: Composition of continuous functions
primary_statement: the composite of continuous functions is continuous

title: Continuous image of a compact set is compact
primary_statement: if f is continuous on compact K then f(K) is compact

title: Extreme value theorem
primary_statement: a continuous function on [a,b] attains a maximum and a minimum

title: Intermediate value theorem
primary_statement: a continuous function on [a,b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b)

title: Uniform continuity
primary_statement: forall eps>0 exists delta>0 forall x,y |x-y|<delta implies |f(x)-f(y)|<eps

title: Heine-Cantor theorem
primary_statement: a continuous function on a compact set is uniformly continuous

title: Continuous image of a connected set is connected
primary_statement: if f is continuous on connected D then f(D) is connected

title: Derivative
primary_statement: f'(c) = lim_{x->c} (f(x)-f(c))/(x-c) when the limit exists

title: Differentiable implies continuous
primary_statement: if f'(c) exists then f is continuous at c

title: Fermat interior extremum theorem
primary_statement: if f has a local extremum at an interior point c and f'(c) exists then f'(c)=0

title: Rolle's theorem
primary_statement: f continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), f(a)=f(b) imply f'(c)=0 for some c

title: Mean value theorem
primary_statement: f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) for some c in (a,b)

title: Monotonicity from the sign of f'
primary_statement: f' >= 0 on an interval implies f is nondecreasing there

title: Cauchy mean value theorem
primary_statement: (f(b)-f(a)) g'(c) = (g(b)-g(a)) f'(c) for some c

title: L'Hopital's rule
primary_statement: lim f/g = lim f'/g' under the 0/0 or inf/inf hypotheses

title: Partition of an interval
primary_statement: a finite set a = t_0 < ... < t_n = b

title: Bounded function
primary_statement: exists M forall x in D |f(x)| <= M

title: Monotone function
primary_statement: nondecreasing or nonincreasing on D

title: Upper and lower Darboux sums
primary_statement: U(f,P) = sum M_i dt_i ; L(f,P) = sum m_i dt_i

title: Riemann integral
primary_statement: the common value of inf_P U(f,P) and sup_P L(f,P) when they are equal

title: Riemann (Cauchy) criterion for integrability
primary_statement: f is integrable iff for every eps>0 some P has U(f,P) - L(f,P) < eps

title: Continuous functions are integrable
primary_statement: a continuous function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable

title: Monotone functions are integrable
primary_statement: a monotone function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable

title: Linearity of the integral
primary_statement: integral of af+bg = a int f + b int g

title: Additivity over intervals
primary_statement: int_a^b = int_a^c + int_c^b

title: Monotonicity of the integral
primary_statement: f <= g implies int f <= int g

title: Integral mean value theorem
primary_statement: int_a^b f = f(c)(b-a) for some c, f continuous

title: Fundamental theorem of calculus, part I
primary_statement: F(x) = int_a^x f is differentiable with F' = f where f is continuous

title: Fundamental theorem of calculus, part II
primary_statement: int_a^b f = G(b) - G(a) for any antiderivative G of an integrable f

title: Integration by parts
primary_statement: int u v' = uv - int u' v

title: Change of variables (substitution)
primary_statement: int_a^b f(g(x)) g'(x) dx = int_{g(a)}^{g(b)} f(u) du

title: Pointwise convergence
primary_statement: f_n(x) -> f(x) for each fixed x in D

title: Uniform convergence
primary_statement: sup_{x in D} |f_n(x) - f(x)| -> 0

title: Uniform Cauchy criterion
primary_statement: f_n converges uniformly iff it is uniformly Cauchy

title: Weierstrass M-test
primary_statement: |f_n| <= M_n and Sigma M_n converges imply Sigma f_n converges uniformly

title: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
primary_statement: if f_n are continuous and f_n -> f uniformly then f is continuous

title: Uniform convergence and integration
primary_statement: if f_n -> f uniformly on [a,b] then int f_n -> int f

title: Uniform convergence and differentiation
primary_statement: if f_n -> f pointwise and f_n' -> g uniformly then f' = g

title: Power series
primary_statement: Sigma a_n (x - c)^n

title: Radius of convergence
primary_statement: 1/R = limsup |a_n|^{1/n} ; converges for |x-c| < R

title: The epsilon-delta / epsilon-N idiom
primary_statement: quantifier order is forall eps exists delta/N
